_comment: Provenance + curation for the Learn-mode "National flags" tab (public/national-flags/).
Every flag a country's tab shows is listed here, with the exact Wikimedia Commons file it
was fetched from, a sha256 of the bundled bytes, the fetch date, and a SOURCED description.
Nothing here is written from memory: dates, names and symbolism all come from the cited
source, exactly like scripts/data/era-flag-sources.json and capital-flag-sources.json.
node scripts/download-national-flags.mjs [--force|--check]   fetch / re-verify the images
node scripts/build-national-flags.mjs                        regenerate src/data/nationalFlags.ts
ENTRY FIELDS
id        stable slug, unique across the whole file (used as the React key and the
meaning-lookup key).
category  historical | official | military | maritime | standard | civilstate | indigenous
name      the flag's own name, as the cited source gives it.
from/to   years the design was in official use (to: 9999 = still current). Historical
entries are ordered newest-first by the generator.
reuse     path (relative to BASE_URL) of a file ALREADY bundled for another feature —
the current national flag (flags/xx.svg) or an era-map flag
(historical-flags/*). This is the link to the historical eras: the same image
and the same window feed both views, and check-national-flags.mjs fails the
build if a reused era flag's window here disagrees with the window in
src/data/historicalFlagValidity.ts.
commons   Commons filename to fetch (entries WITHOUT `reuse`), bundled at
public/national-flags/<file>.
design    what the image is — shown as the card's sub-label.
meaning   sourced "What this flag means" explainer { description, myths?, sources[] }.
source    authoritative URL for the name/dates.
CURATION RULES
1. `historical` covers the flags of THIS state (and the predecessor states centred on
the same territory, e.g. the Empire of Brazil, the Ottoman Empire). A colonial
ruler's own flag is NOT a national flag of the colony — the era maps already show
that, captioned as the ruler's flag, and it must never be listed here as if the
territory's own.
2. `military` is service-level flags (army, navy, air force, marine corps) only —
never rank, command or appointment flags, of which there are hundreds.
3. Never invent a flag, a date, or a meaning. A flag with no sourced symbolism ships
with no `meaning` rather than a guessed one.

flags.name: Provisional flag of the Republic (15–19 November 1889)
flags.design: Thirteen green and yellow stripes with 21 white stars in a blue canton — flown for four days after the proclamation of the republic.

meaning.description: Raised on 15 November 1889, the day the republic was proclaimed, this flag closely copied the flag of the United States — thirteen stripes and a starred canton — as a deliberate statement that Brazil was now a federal republic on the American model. Deodoro da Fonseca rejected it four days later precisely because it imitated another nation's flag, and the green-and-yellow field of the imperial flag was kept instead, so that the change of regime did not read as a change of country.

flags.name: Flag of the Empire of Brazil

flags.name: Naval jack (Bandeira do Cruzeiro)
flags.design: Dark blue with 21 white stars in a cross — 13 across and 9 down.

meaning.description: The jack flown at the bow of Brazilian warships shows the Southern Cross constellation, from which the flag takes its name, and 21 stars for the provinces of the empire at the time it was adopted in 1847. It is the oldest Brazilian flag still in use, having survived both the fall of the empire and every redrawing of the national flag's star field.

flags.name: Australian Aboriginal Flag
flags.design: Black over red with a yellow disc at the centre; proclaimed a Flag of Australia in 1995.

meaning.description: Harold Thomas designed the flag in 1971 for the land-rights movement and gave each element a meaning: the black upper half represents the Aboriginal people of Australia, the red lower half the red earth and the ochre used in ceremony, and the yellow disc the sun, the giver of life. It was proclaimed a Flag of Australia in July 1995, and in January 2022 the Commonwealth acquired the copyright so that it can be reproduced freely.

omitted.name: Torres Strait Islander Flag
omitted.reason: The third flag proclaimed under the Flags Act is still under copyright (held for the Torres Strait Island Regional Council), so no freely-licensed file exists on Wikimedia Commons — en.wikipedia itself shows a placeholder in its place. Bundling a non-free image is not an option, and this repo never approximates a flag, so it is honestly absent until a free file exists.

independence.event: The six colonies federated as the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January 1901.
independence.note: Legislative independence was completed later, by the Statute of Westminster (adopted 1942) and the Australia Acts of 1986.

flags.name: Union Flag
flags.design: The crosses of St George, St Andrew and St Patrick combined — the design adopted when Ireland joined the union on 1 January 1801.

meaning.description: The Union Flag layers three patron saints' crosses in the order the kingdoms joined: England's red cross of St George on white, Scotland's white saltire of St Andrew on blue (joined at the union of the crowns in 1606) and the red saltire of St Patrick for Ireland, added when the Kingdom of Ireland joined the union in 1801. St Patrick's saltire is set counterchanged — offset from the centre of the white Scottish saltire — so that neither saltire appears to take precedence over the other, which is why the flag is not symmetrical and can be flown upside down.

flags.name: Flag of the Kingdom of Great Britain

flags.name: Flag of South Africa
flags.design: A horizontal Y in green, fimbriated white and gold, separating red and blue from a black triangle at the hoist.

meaning.description: Designed by State Herald Frederick Brownell and first flown on 27 April 1994, the day of the first democratic election, the flag was drawn to carry no per-colour symbolism at all — the only South African national flag whose design has no official meaning attached to its colours. What the design does say is said by its shape: the horizontal Y, or pall, shows two paths converging into one, which the government describes as the convergence of diverse elements within South African society taking the road ahead in unity.

flags.design: A white field bearing the assembly's seal.

flags.name: Flag of India (Tiranga)
flags.design: A horizontal tricolour of saffron, white and green with the navy-blue Ashoka Chakra of 24 spokes at the centre; adopted 22 July 1947.

flags.name: Flag of the Indian Armed Forces
flags.commons: Flag of the Indian Armed Forces.svg
flags.design: A horizontal tricolour of red, navy blue and sky blue — one colour for each service — with the tri-service crest.

flags.name: Indian Naval Ensign
flags.design: A white field with the national flag in the canton and the navy's octagonal crest in the fly, adopted in 2022.

flags.name: Civil ensign of India
flags.design: A Red Ensign with the national flag in the canton, flown by Indian merchant ships.

flags.name: State ensign of India
flags.design: A Blue Ensign with the national flag in the canton and a yellow anchor.

flags.name: Presidential Standard of India (1950–1971)
flags.commons: Flag of the President of India (1950–1971).svg
flags.design: Quartered dark blue: the Lions of Sarnath, an elephant, a pair of scales and a lotus vase — discontinued in 1971 in favour of the national flag.

flags.name: Union Flag
flags.design: The Union Flag, the official flag over British India from the Crown's assumption of rule in 1858 until independence.

flags.name: Star of India Red Ensign
flags.design: A Red Ensign defaced with the Star of India — the ensign associated with British India, though the Union Flag was the official flag.

flags.name: Flag of the British East India Company
flags.commons: Flag of the British East India Company (1801).svg
flags.design: Red and white stripes with the Union Flag in the canton, flown by the company that ruled much of India until the Crown took over in 1858.

independence.event: Independence and partition under the Indian Independence Act, 15 August 1947.

flags.name: Flag of the People's Republic of China
flags.design: A red field with one large gold star and four smaller stars in an arc, hoisted on 1 October 1949.

flags.name: Flag of the Republic of China (1928–1949)
flags.commons: Flag of the Republic of China.svg
flags.design: The Blue Sky with a White Sun in the canton of a red field — the national flag of China from the Northern Expedition until 1949.

flags.name: Flag of the Republic of China (1912–1928)
flags.design: The Five-Races-Under-One-Union flag: red, yellow, blue, white and black stripes for the Han, Manchu, Mongol, Hui and Tibetan peoples.

flags.name: Yellow Dragon Flag of the Qing dynasty
flags.design: A rectangular yellow field with a blue dragon chasing a red pearl. The triangular version dates from 1862; before that China had no national flag.

flags.name: Flag of the People's Liberation Army
flags.commons: Flag of the People's Liberation Army.svg
flags.design: A red field with a gold star and the characters 八一 for 1 August, the date of the 1927 Nanchang uprising.

flags.name: Ensign of the PLA Ground Force
flags.commons: Ground Force Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg
flags.design: The PLA flag with a green stripe along the bottom.

flags.name: Ensign of the PLA Navy
flags.design: The PLA flag with blue and white stripes along the bottom.

flags.name: Ensign of the PLA Air Force
flags.commons: Air Force Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg
flags.design: The PLA flag with a sky-blue stripe along the bottom.

flags.name: Ensign of the PLA Rocket Force
flags.commons: Rocket Force Flag of the People's Republic of China.svg
flags.design: The PLA flag with a gold-and-blue stripe along the bottom.
